newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.79/80, RBI buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.79/80, RBI buys dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained against the dollar, breaching the 35.80-mark on Thursday, dealers said.
"There were deals upto 35.7925," said a dealer at a foreign bank. He said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stepped in towards the close, buying dollars at 35.79/80 levels.
Large inward remittances and a tapering off of month-end dollar demand led to the rupee's rise, dealers said.
Spot rupee opened at 35.815/825 but the rupee kept rising because of poor demand. The State Bank of India (SBI), the major dollar buyer in recent days, kept bidding down, dealers said.
The rupee gained against the forward dollar too as many banks received premiums against forward dollar sales.
The annualised six month premium closed at 4.58 percent compared with the previous close of 4.75 percent.
"The premiums opened high on fears of fund shortage driving call money rates but fell later," said a dealer.
Fears of fund shortage were caused by an outflow of 30 billion rupees towards a three-year bond on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected subdued dollar demand amid good supplies to continue in the next few days.
